To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

genome-wide association studies in mouse inbreed strains are prone to false-positive results, that linkage analysis is necessary to validate the association, and that the Lasc1 gene is not a functional element in the mouse lung tumor system.
GWA studies carried out in mouse inbred strain panels can have a very high rate of false positive loci, and that linkage mapping in intercross populations is necessary to validate the results.

GWA in inbred mouse strain panels can yield false-positive results that are not replicated in independent mouse populations and that GWA should be used in combination with genetic linkage analysis in mouse crosses.
